races.name: Knockcroghery Claiming Hurdle

runners_data.name: Getaway Charlie
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old whose recent form reads four consecutive non-completions or poor finishes; Timothy Doyle yard is 0/4 in the last 14 days and 83 days off a run — his natural game is racing prominently but the number of pace-minded rivals here means he's unlikely to find his ideal pitch, and that form string offers little encouragement regardless.

runners_data.name: Paul Collins
runners_data.note: Back six days after his last run and wearing a hood, this six-year-old won over 2m2f on Good but has struggled badly on Soft and in more competitive company since; inclined to race forward by nature yet likely to be shuffled wider in the pack with multiple rivals seeking early position ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Howya
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie and a visor flag a horse that needs everything to go right; trainer Queally is 2/6 in the last 14 days suggesting current form, and this ten-year-old has two wins on Good ground — the medium-to-short trip history (20-23f) means 3m is a slight question, but he tends to travel sweetly in touch and could be dangerous if the trip is within range.

runners_data.name: Tullyveery Lad
runners_data.note: Blinkers on, Darragh O'Keeffe in the plate — a combination that demands respect — and his 15-from-15 runs on Good going record is the most compelling figure in the race; two wins and five places from similar conditions, plus multiple runs at this distance band, mark him as the archetype this pace shape could suit if he settles close enough to Howdoyalikeherhome.

runners_data.name: Howdoyalikeherhome
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's seven-year-old is the sole front-runner and arrives just six days after his last run, wearing tongue-tie and blinkers; he is genuinely pace-dominant in this field but the quick turnaround and a style-fit flag suggest he is racing slightly out of optimum role — his chance hinges on whether the short recovery blunts his stamina in the final mile.

runners_data.name: Bocelli's Voice
runners_data.note: McLoughlin is 0/11 in the last 14 days, the mare is ten, and her last five runs on similar or faster going have produced one place from 12 starts; a true hold-up type pushed into a midfield slot on the map because the rear is crowded — her finishing thrust has been repeatedly absent and this trip (longest she's faced) is unproven.

runners_data.name: Garnetot
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at five, this Elliott-trained gelding showed a promising second on Good over 2m but fell on his most recent qualifying run and finished out of the frame on Good last time; he maps as a hold-up horse over what is a career-longest 3m trip — interesting long-term, but the fall and stamina query are real flags here.

runners_data.name: Live My Dream
runners_data.note: Has not completed three of his last six starts, the visor is new headgear, and his best form has come over shorter trips (16-19f) — stepping up to 3m looks like a significant ask; lowest weight in the race at 146lbs and a 73-day break means condition is uncertain, and Josh Williamson's claiming allowance may be his principal asset.

races.paceDynamic: Howdoyalikeherhome is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to contest the lead, will stride into an uncontested position from the outset over this 3m trip on Good ground at Roscommon. That lone-leader setup creates a sustainable, controlled pace — one that rewards a horse travelling comfortably in mid-division and picking up when the race quickens from the third-last. The field carries more prominent types than the shape can accommodate: Getaway Charlie, Paul Collins, and Bocelli's Voice are genuine pace/hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because Howdoyalikeherhome, Rocky's Howya, and Tullyveery Lad are the horses most likely to actually secure prominent positions behind the leader. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner setting a fair but manageable tempo over 3m — most favours a prominent or tracking horse with strong Good-ground form who can travel within striking range and assert from the home turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Howdoyalikeherhome Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Howdoyalikeherhome leads unchallenged and the tempo stays honest enough to stretch the field before the final flight.
scenarios.body: Howdoyalikeherhome dictates from the front, controls the fractions, and punishes any challenger who has used energy to get prominent; a lone leader on Good ground over 3m with no serious pace pressure is a potent scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Howdoyalikeherhome's recent back-to-back runs in six days leave a chink and a tracking horse delivers from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Howya or Tullyveery Lad, both with solid Good-ground form and proven winners at this trip range, pounce from just off the pace in the final two flights; Tullyveery Lad in particular has a 15/15 similar-going record and multiple course-distance wins to call on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Pressure Scrambles Order
scenarios.trigger: If Getaway Charlie or Paul Collins push forward aggressively early and force a contested lead that heightens the tempo.
scenarios.body: A quicker early pace would stretch the field and leave the front group vulnerable, opening the door for a hold-up horse like Garnetot or Live My Dream to stay on past tiring rivals late; however both are lightly-credentialled at this trip and on this track, limiting this scenario's probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Benefit From Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent brigade burns itself out and late-finishing hold-up types sweep through beaten horses from the rear.
scenarios.body: Bocelli's Voice and Live My Dream are genuine hold-up types but both carry poor recent form, low RPRs, and questionable jumping records; this shape can only materialise if the pace genuinely unravels, which a single uncontested front-runner is unlikely to produce.

watchPoints.text: Tullyveery Lad — watch whether Darragh O'Keeffe slots him just off Howdoyalikeherhome's heels from the outset; if he travels smoothly in second or third through the back straight his Good-ground dominance and blinkers make him the primary danger to the leader.

Howdoyalikeherhome — monitor his jumping under Danny Gilligan in the early stages; a horse racing on a six-day turnaround who has already run twice recently may show signs of fatigue from the third-last, which would trigger Scenario B immediately.

Rocky's Howya — Kevin Healy's 7lb claim is meaningful over 3m and the horse has winning form at shorter distances on Good; watch whether the trip stretch catches him out from two out, as he may be in the race until the final flight and then flatten.

Getaway Charlie and Paul Collins — both natural front-runners likely to be shuffled back early; if either pushes forward to contest the lead against Howdoyalikeherhome in the first mile, the tempo will lift and the entire race shape shifts toward Scenario C, which would benefit the genuine hold-up horses at the rear.

Garnetot — watch his jumping at the early flights given his recent fall; if he pings hurdles cleanly under Paddy Cleary he could sit closer than his hold-up tag suggests, but any hesitation early will leave him too far back over this demanding 3m trip.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Acheron
runners_data.note: Interesting handicap mark of OR 105 for John Joseph Hanlon's hold-up type, placed twice in Good ground but carries a redistribution caveat — its natural station is at the rear, not the midfield shown, meaning it may not get the strong pace it needs to produce its best finish; STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Casper Charlie
runners_data.note: Una Corcoran runner returning after 65 days with a single run showing a finish position of 13th on Good ground; hold-up style with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish makes it hard to recommend in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Cooladdi
runners_data.note: Eoghan Finegan (claimer) rides this Conor Maxwell prominent racer who has placed twice in five Good-ground starts including a second over today's trip; the headgear (hood) is notable and the 23-day turnaround suits, making this a logical pace-tracking danger.

runners_data.name: Frankie's Freebie
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner for Adrian Sexton and apprentice Harry Sexton — five consecutive placed efforts including two seconds in similar trips show genuine consistency, though best form has come on softer ground and the Good surface has produced only one placed run from seven.

runners_data.name: Fuusland
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends this lightly-raced 5yo for whom there is no historical hurdle data; the UNKNOWN going tag and debut-level uncertainty mean this is a pure unknown, though the stable's record with unexposed hurdlers demands respect.

runners_data.name: Go To The Moon
runners_data.note: Mark McNiff's hold-up 6yo returns after 55 days with just one run over hurdles, showing a finish of 12th on Good; a fade-in-finish flag and minimal jumping evidence make this a risk at this stage of its career.

runners_data.name: Imarajan
runners_data.note: Eoin Doyle's consistent prominent racer has eight runs on Good ground with four placed efforts, including a recent second over similar distances; the tongue-tie headgear is present, the 36-day break is fine, and the profile fits a slowly-run race where a close tracker can pounce off the final bend.

runners_data.name: Killowen House
runners_data.note: Paul Gilligan (T14: 1/13) has a runner returning 27 days after its last start with an unknown style tag but a placed effort over 24f on Good ground last time; the form figures of P61-37 show some inconsistency but the 24f good-ground placed run is exactly the trip profile needed here.

runners_data.name: Little Big John
runners_data.note: Maike Magnussen's 5yo is tagged unknown style with hood headgear; two Good-ground runs show a best of 6th and the form figures of P0-6 point to a horse still finding its level — limited encouragement for a 15-runner field.

runners_data.name: Blue Nude
runners_data.note: PJ Rothwell's lightly-raced 4yo is a genuine hold-up type placed into midfield on the map because the field is overloaded with closers; one career run showing 16th on Good is the only evidence and the fade-in-finish flag adds concern — its true position at the rear may leave it with too much to do.

runners_data.name: Take The Free
runners_data.note: E Bolger's 4yo was second on its most recent start (soft, 16f) and holds a reasonable form string of 8-6-2; a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield means it races out of its preferred role, and while the second suggests talent, the pace scenario does not suit.

runners_data.name: Lilac Lady
runners_data.note: Mark McNiff's consistent mare has four placed efforts from 15 Good-ground runs and a tongue-tie; she is a natural hold-up runner shown in midfield only because of redistribution pressure — her best chance comes if the pace develops strongly, which is not the likely scenario with one front-runner.

runners_data.name: Midnight Musical
runners_data.note: Anthony McCann's 5yo ran just three days ago, raising obvious fitness questions; hold-up style with a fade-in-finish flag and a career best of 5th in Good conditions — the quick turnaround is the primary concern here.

runners_data.name: Online Order
runners_data.note: Liam Cusack's 7-year-old making its handicap debut with only one run on record (7th on soft, 16f) and hood headgear; the hold-up profile and lack of any Good-ground evidence make this extremely hard to assess.

runners_data.name: Sea Feliz
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends this lightly-raced 5yo hurdler with no historical data — UNKNOWN going, debut, and the biggest question mark in the field; Mullins' strike rate with unexposed hurdlers on Good ground at provincial tracks demands the horse is not dismissed entirely despite zero form evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Frankie's Freebie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner maiden hurdle over 2m4½f at Roscommon on Good ground, meaning the pace is almost certain to be set by one horse without serious pressure from the front. With no rival willing to contest the lead, Frankie's Freebie can dictate a relaxed, even gallop through the early stages — a tempo that is sustainable but unlikely to stretch the field until the home straight. This shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader at close range and pounce in the final two flights, rather than genuine hold-up horses who need a strong pace to close into. The field does contain more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Acheron, Blue Nude, Take The Free, and Lilac Lady are all true hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map, meaning Cooladdi and Imarajan are the prominent types best placed to exploit a front-runner who is not being pressured.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Frankie's Freebie Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Frankie's Freebie is allowed to control an uncontested lead and sets a steady, measured gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Frankie's Freebie finds the Good ground to its liking, jumps cleanly, and builds momentum from the front without ever being asked to sprint — consistent form of 2-2-4-2-2 shows it stays competitive at this trip. The prominent trackers sitting just behind in second and third will have first run on the closers, making early-movers off the pace the chief danger.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace set by Frankie's Freebie allows a close-tracking prominent runner to cruise through and overwhelm the leader from two out.
scenarios.body: A relaxed gallop means a horse settled just off the lead travels well within itself and arrives full of running at the second-last, needing only to jump cleanly to go clear. Imarajan's consistent placed form in Good-ground conditions and Cooladdi's staying profile both suit a race where the early pace is unhurried and fitness counts late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens unexpectedly or front-runners tire, opening a gap for a hold-up finisher to close strongly from the final flight.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a genuine strong gallop to develop, which is unlikely given only one front-runner, but a hold-up runner mapping to midfield could still benefit if Frankie's Freebie fades sharply. Acheron (OR 105, sim-going form) and Take The Free (second last time, 4yo) carry the most credible late profiles though their redistribution to midfield weakens the case.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Talent Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed or debut hurdlers from top yards produces a step forward that overwhelms the moderate early pace.
scenarios.body: Sea Feliz (W P Mullins, debut hurdler) and Fuusland (Gordon Elliott, lightly raced) are completely unknown quantities whose flat/bumper ability could translate instantly. The pace-scenario does not suit them structurally, but a dominant talent can override any shape — assign only residual probability here given the lack of evidence.

watchPoints.text: Watch Frankie's Freebie at the start — if it jumps cleanly and immediately sets an uncontested lead, the race shape is locked in and prominent trackers become the primary danger to it; any hesitation at the first could disrupt the entire tactical picture.

Imarajan and Cooladdi will both want to be prominent early in a 15-runner field — if they get crowded or lose their position in the first mile, their chance is significantly undermined in what is set to be a slowly-run race.

Acheron, Take The Free, and Blue Nude are all genuine hold-up types mapped to midfield — monitor where they actually settle in running, as horses forced to race against their style in a slowly-run race are particularly at risk of never getting competitive.

Sea Feliz (Mullins, debut) and Fuusland (Elliott, lightly raced) are complete unknowns — any significant market move at the off should be noted as yard intelligence may be strong on unexposed hurdlers of this type.

Midnight Musical ran only three days ago — watch its behaviour in the pre-parade ring and how freely it settles early, as a quick turnaround on Good ground over this trip is an unusual preparation and energy levels may be compromised.

races.name: Shanagher Hearing Maiden Hurdle (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Firebrand
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form including two second-place finishes on Good ground over this exact 2m trip; prominent style suits the expected pace shape, and headgear (tp) suggests connections are targeting a win, but has yet to convert seven placed efforts from similar positions.

runners_data.name: Cocofred
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's runner has the strongest trainer 14-day strike rate in this field (11/35) and holds solid form credentials, but is a natural hold-up horse whose true style is squeezed by the volume of closers in this field — likely to find himself further forward than ideal without the cover he needs.

runners_data.name: Glengarriff
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a dire recent record including finishing 18th and 13th on Good ground; the fade-in-finish flag reinforces a pattern of weakening late, and Patrick O'Brien claiming 5lb cannot disguise limited ability here.

runners_data.name: Lengaruka
runners_data.note: Completely unknown quantity on debut with no public form data and an unknown going preference; the lightly raced flag and stable's modest 14-day figures (0/3) make this an impossible profile to rate without further information.

runners_data.name: Luker's Tipple
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's prominent-style runner has been placed six times in 15 runs and twice hit the frame over this 2m trip on Good ground; Conor Stone-Walsh has strong form connections with this yard and the horse's consistent tracking style ideally suits a Game Point-controlled tempo.

runners_data.name: Ozark's Walk
runners_data.note: Long 111-day absence and a fade-in-finish tendency make this hold-up horse a significant risk; did place twice in Good-ground conditions earlier but recent form (0 last run, dash last time) is uninspiring and the layoff adds a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Sunny Dude
runners_data.note: Consistent fader who has failed to place in all seven comparable Good-ground runs and has a stark fade-in-finish tendency; the 7lb apprentice claim does not compensate for a pattern of tail-end finishes in this sort of company.

runners_data.name: Tellyouwhat
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only one run to assess over this exact trip on Good, pulled up on debut; Edward Mitchell's yard has a blank 14-day record and there is insufficient evidence to project a meaningful chance.

runners_data.name: Finjimk
runners_data.note: Has fallen and been pulled up in his career, then finished seventh on only run over this course and trip; Peter Flood's yard returns modest recent figures and the lightly raced flag combined with jumping errors makes this a difficult profile to endorse.

runners_data.name: Game Point
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for a yard with a recent winner in the past fortnight, and Game Point is the race's confirmed pace-setter — however the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) notes he is rated as prominent rather than a pure front-runner and the headgear (h) may indicate a need for restraint that slightly compromises his controlling role.

runners_data.name: Astelia
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey's seven-year-old is the most experienced prominent racer in the field with seven place finishes, three of them on Good ground over 2m; Sam Ewing takes the ride and Astelia's profile of tracking quietly and challenging late off a slow pace is directly suited to a Game Point-dominated shape.

runners_data.name: How's Ellie
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins runner returning after a long 223-day absence; both career hurdle runs produced fifth-place finishes and the hold-up style is workable, but fitness after a seven-month break is the dominant concern here despite the yard's pedigree.

runners_data.name: Poetic Parable
runners_data.note: Debuting hurdler from Ross O'Sullivan's yard with no public form; the yard's 14-day record is 0/10, which tempers expectations, and the unknown going profile means this is pure speculation unless significant stable confidence emerges.

runners_data.name: Dadou Part Two
runners_data.note: Well-held on debut (11th) and absent 109 days; a natural hold-up horse who is mapped to midfield by necessity rather than preference — the fade-in-finish flag and redistribution together mean the scenario in which he wins requires things to go very wrong for rivals ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Pretty Wild
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden is a high-profile booking for E. Bolger's debutant and that jockey–trainer combination warrants respect; completely unexposed with no form to assess, but a capable jumps jockey taking the ride from the off signals that connections believe there is ability to exploit here.

races.paceDynamic: Game Point is the one confirmed front-runner and, with Jack Kennedy aboard for a yard with a live recent strike rate, is expected to stride into a clear lead from the outset and control tempo on Good ground at Roscommon over 2m. The field is large at 15 runners but the pace map places only Game Point as a genuine leader, meaning the gallop should be measured and sustainable rather than searingly contested — a rhythm that rewards horses who can track closely and strike off the bend. Prominent racers Firebrand, Luker's Tipple, and Astelia are best placed to press behind Game Point and exploit any slowing of the tempo in the straight. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Cocofred and Dadou Part Two are natural hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map, meaning they are unlikely to get ideal cover and their true closing style is compromised — this race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent/tracking runners who can sit just off the pace and challenge from the second-last hurdle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Game Point Controls Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Game Point leads unchallenged and sets a steady, uncontested rhythm that suits horses making smooth headway from prominent positions.
scenarios.body: Game Point's lone front-running role on Good ground over 2m creates a falsely run race where those tracking within two lengths hold a decisive positional advantage turning for home; horses who can travel fluently close to the pace and jump cleanly will have first run at the final hurdles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Battles Out
scenarios.trigger: If Firebrand, Luker's Tipple, and Astelia all push forward aggressively to sit alongside or immediately behind Game Point, creating a genuine pace battle from the front.
scenarios.body: The contested gallop stretches the field early and exposes stamina reserves, with the strongest stayer among the prominent runners grinding out a narrow advantage on the run-in; a horse with both tactical speed and jumping accuracy benefits most in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically late and hold-up horses find daylight through a tiring field in the final 2 hurdles.
scenarios.body: This shape relies on Cocofred or Dadou Part Two finding room from midfield — both are redistributed from their natural hold-up positions and unlikely to be ideally placed; the scenario is possible but structurally compromised given neither can realistically get to the rear as they would prefer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets Field
scenarios.trigger: If an unexposed or lightly raced runner like Pretty Wild, Poetic Parable, or Lengaruka takes to hurdling quickly and outclasses this modest maiden field.
scenarios.body: An unknown quantity with flat or point-to-point breeding who handles Good ground and settles into a prominent position could pick off tired rivals late; the lightly raced fillies and debutants carry genuine upside risk that form-lines cannot fully price.

watchPoints.text: Game Point (Jack Kennedy) — if he bowls into an uncontested lead at a crawl, the first two horses in his slipstream at the second-last hurdle are best placed to pounce; watch whether Astelia or Luker's Tipple can get on terms turning for home.

Cocofred (Darragh O'Keeffe) — a natural hold-up horse likely to be placed further forward than ideal; watch whether O'Keeffe attempts to drop him in regardless, which would leave him out of position and unable to deliver his closing run.

Pretty Wild (Harry Cobden) — a high-profile jockey booking on an unknown debutant from E. Bolger's yard; any strong market move before the off should be treated seriously as it may reflect stable confidence not visible in the form.

How's Ellie (Brian Hayes, Mullins) — a 223-day absence is the single biggest fitness risk in this field; watch the paddock and opening market moves to gauge whether Mullins has her fully ready to run a big race first time back.

Dadou Part Two and Ozark's Walk — both are genuine hold-up types with fade tendencies, long absences, and compromised positional fits; if either is backed against the trend, it may signal that connections expect a strong gallop to develop and turn this into a true staying test.

races.name: SuperValu Co. Roscommon Ladies Day Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Dani Donadoni
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained and clearly the race-shaper here; OR 130 is comfortably the highest in the field and sim-going figures (5/8, 1W2P) are solid on Good, but the STYLE_FIT flag means the chance is tempered if the race shape doesn't allow a clean lead.|

runners_data.name: Endless Talking
runners_data.note: Two wins on the bounce coming in (form: 11), both on Good ground at 16f-19f, suggesting this trip and surface suit perfectly; Cromwell's stable is firing (T14: 8/47) and Donoghue's booking is a clear upgrade, making this one of the more compelling prominent profiles in the field.|

runners_data.name: The Store Boy
runners_data.note: De Bromhead has him fit (41 days, T14: 9/41) and the horse's latest win was over 16f on Good — identical conditions today — but his natural front-running instinct is squeezed by the presence of Dani Donadoni, meaning he may race in a more restrained position than ideal for his style.|

runners_data.name: Move It On Over
runners_data.note: Runs in a hood and carries a persistent fade flag backed up by a form string of 98-080; genuinely a hold-up type by inclination yet bumped to a mapped midfield slot, meaning both style and recent form work against him here on Good ground.|

runners_data.name: Suresuresure
runners_data.note: Two fade warnings and a form line (88P-07) that offers little encouragement; the trainer has had zero winners from three runners in the past fortnight, and while the horse has experience on Good ground it has never threatened to win on that surface.|

runners_data.name: Whoyougonnacall
runners_data.note: Very lightly raced over hurdles (only two hurdles runs in the form book), carries a fade flag and has shown nothing in either start — a 5lb claimer in the saddle adds another layer of risk for a horse that needs to find significant improvement.|

runners_data.name: Lizzie Twigg
runners_data.note: Elliott's 5lb claimer partnership has already landed two wins from three starts (form: 15-1) and both victories came on Good ground at 16f-18f — conditions replicated precisely today; fresh after 30 days and clearly progressive, this mare profiles as one of the safest prominent-style beneficiaries if the race runs to shape.|

races.paceDynamic: Dani Donadoni is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novice hurdle and should bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested clip on Good ground at Roscommon, setting a genuine but manageable tempo throughout. Endless Talking and Lizzie Twigg are the most natural prominent riders who will look to sit just off the pace and apply pressure from the second flight onward, while The Store Boy is a genuine prominent type who may find himself nudged back toward midfield simply because the competition for those forward berths is stiff. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position — Dani Donadoni and Endless Talking are most likely to actually hold the lead and the prominent slot respectively, with The Store Boy and Move It On Over absorbing positions further back than ideal. With a single honest pace-setter dictating from the front and no pressure to force an unsustainable gallop, this shape strongly favours prominent-to-handy runners who can track the leader comfortably and quicken off a sound jumping rhythm — hold-up horses will need a strong pace injection that simply may not materialise here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Dani Donadoni sets a controlled, uncontested lead and the race is run at a fair but non-frenetic clip throughout.
scenarios.body: Dani Donadoni dictates from the front without a challenge, allowing prominent chasers to travel sweetly in behind; the winner comes from the front two or three approaching the last, with jumping ability and class the decisive factors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Compounds, Chaser Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Dani Donadoni sets a slightly stronger gallop than is sustainable and weakens approaching the final flight.
scenarios.body: The race opens up from two out as the leader fades and a prominent or handy tracker swoops to the front; a horse who has settled smoothly in second or third benefits most from the leader's capitulation.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Late Flourish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is unusually steady and the race turns into a sprint from the second-last flight.
scenarios.body: A compressed field with few separated by distance means hold-up horses can suddenly produce a late run; however, Suresuresure and Whoyougonnacall carry poor recent form and the fade warnings limit confidence in this shape materialising cleanly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Incident Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If a fall, unseating or jumping error among the prominent horses reshuffles the field mid-race.
scenarios.body: A runner carrying baggage — Whoyougonnacall's very limited experience and Move It On Over's form trough — could create a gap that a survivor exploits; this is a low-probability chaos scenario rather than a clean pace shape.

watchPoints.text: Lizzie Twigg's jumping under pressure — both wins came with clean rounds and any error at a crucial flight could cost her the prominent position her form demands.

The Store Boy's early positioning — if he tries to assert and crowd Dani Donadoni for the lead in the first half-mile, it could force an untypical pace and unsettle the expected race shape for prominent runners.

Whoyougonnacall's jumping experience — with only two hurdles starts and a fall in the form string, Liam Quinlan will need to give this horse every chance to find a rhythm and avoid a jumping blunder that disrupts the field.

Dani Donadoni's jumping quality is worth monitoring from the outset — if the Mullins runner meets a flight wrong early, the uncontested lead scenario collapses and the race loses its shape-setter entirely.

Move It On Over's headgear (hood) and fade flag together suggest watching whether J J Slevin can keep him engaged mid-race — if he drops away before the last two flights the field compresses and the finish could tighten unpredictably.

races.name: Sheehy Meares/Team Earley Handicap Hurdle (0-100)

runners_data.name: Eyeeye
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 100, genuine hold-up style with course form at this trip on Good, apprentice rider Jack Gilligan claims 5lb; placed twice in similar company recently and goes well fresh (27 days off).

runners_data.name: Whispering Willow
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing type for Gavin Cromwell who has won over this exact C&D on Good going; Keith Donoghue takes the ride and the horse boasts an 8-from-8 placed/won record at sim-going — very strong profile here.

runners_data.name: Walk On Annilog
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner wearing hood, 40 days since last run; limited form at this track and best placing at Good was a fourth — needs everything to go right from the back to feature.

runners_data.name: Patty O'Farrell
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing tongue-tie who landed a recent 2nd on Good over 2m — course-going form stands up, and Danny Gilligan takes the mount; has found it hard to win (1 win from last 13 Good-ground runs) but consistent for place claims.

runners_data.name: Annie's Angel
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for Adrian McGuinness, though tagged STYLE_FIT at 0.92 for racing out of role as a front-runner; the 4yo has limited Good-going form (0 wins, 0 places from 5 sim-going runs) and is dropping back from hurdle starts over further.

runners_data.name: Slowdownbarney
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Dermot McLoughlin wearing tongue-tie; poor recent form (8th last time at this trip on Good) and a modest sim-going record of 0 wins from 3 relevant runs makes improvement hard to project.

runners_data.name: Victoria Kesia
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for John Joseph Hanlon (also trains Urban War), Harry Sexton claims 7lb; showed a third at this trip on Good and has the placing record to suggest she can be competitive in a steadily-run race.

runners_data.name: Walk Win
runners_data.note: Hold-up type flagged as fading in the finish — a pattern that is hard to ignore in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to bring her into it; won at 2m on Good but TS and form have regressed.

runners_data.name: Copper Rocker
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe takes a ride on this 4yo who is a natural hold-up runner but finds itself squeezed into midfield by the sheer number of back-markers in this field; carries a fade flag and STYLE_FIT discount, limiting realistic expectations.

runners_data.name: Cool Summer
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type in truth, wearing hood, but the volume of similar runners forces a midfield mapping here; has placed once in sim-going and showed a third at this C&D — capable of outrunning odds if the race opens up.

runners_data.name: Gentle Annie
runners_data.note: Style unknown with a fade flag, wearing tongue strap and breast girth; showed a third on Good over 2m for Terence O'Brien but the overall profile is inconsistent and Michael Kenneally's claim doesn't fully compensate.

runners_data.name: Del Boys Diva
runners_data.note: A true rear-of-field type that is unlikely to secure its preferred position in a 19-runner field; wearing tongue-tie and a string of 0s in recent form, 0 wins from 4 relevant sim-going runs — evidence is firmly against.

runners_data.name: Highland Earl
runners_data.note: The most interesting of the redistributed hold-up types — won last time out over 17f on Good (365 days ago), so freshness is a genuine concern, but Brian Hayes takes the ride and a 1W/1P sim-going record is solid if rusty.

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: Arriving from a flat code (STA wins over 12f) and making a jumps switch; the stable (McConnell T14=3/22) has some form of late, but 290 days off and flat-track form makes this a large step into the unknown over hurdles on Good.

runners_data.name: China Grill
runners_data.note: Consistent back-end finisher with three consecutive double-figure placings on Good ground over 2m; the fade flag and a 0W/0P record across all three sim-going runs leave little encouragement — mapped to midfield but even that may flatter.

runners_data.name: Dontdooddson
runners_data.note: A 13-year-old prominent-style runner for Darren Collins — the veteran has winning form on Good and manages his 140lb weight well, but the age and a 7-from-7 recent finishing record make winning hard to envisage.

runners_data.name: Gold Gatewood
runners_data.note: Absent 405 days and wearing tongue-tie; only three runs over hurdles, 0 wins, and 0 places in sim-going — Norman Lee has a quiet yard (T14: 0/3) and this is a hard horse to back on return from such a lengthy absence.

runners_data.name: Urban War
runners_data.note: Hanlon's second string, a true hold-up type pushed forward on the map by field congestion; 8-year-old wearing tongue-tie with 0 wins in 15 Good-ground runs and a poor sim-going record — place prospects are slim.

runners_data.name: Goin'
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for A J Martin (T14: 0/4), unlisted jockey; showed a 5th last time at 19f on Good, with two previous placed efforts in sim-going — better over further and on softer ground, but not without some residual interest at the back of the market.

races.paceDynamic: Annie's Angel is the confirmed front-runner and will likely dictate from the outset on Good ground at Roscommon over 2m, setting a sustainable, uncontested tempo that suits horses who can travel prominently and challenge from the home turn. Whispering Willow and Victoria Kesia are the natural prominent racers best positioned to sit just off the pace and pounce, while Dontdooddson can also slot in behind the leader. With 19 runners and a compressed field, there is significant overcrowding toward the rear — Copper Rocker, Urban War, Cool Summer, Del Boys Diva, Highland Earl, Syosset, China Grill and Gold Gatewood are all genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because they cannot all secure their preferred back-of-the-field position in a race this shape, meaning several will be racing outside their natural role. The steady, sustainable gallop set by a single front-runner on Good ground at this track strongly favours horses who can sit prominently or just off the pace and produce a measured late kick — hold-up horses relying on a strong end-to-end gallop to get competitive will find conditions too comfortable up front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Annie's Angel sets a fair clip and Whispering Willow or Victoria Kesia travel smoothly in second or third throughout.
scenarios.body: Annie's Angel controls fractions from the front while the prominent-styleed chasers conserve energy before pressing on the home turn; on Good ground at 2m this is the most efficient tactical position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the final mile and a well-placed hold-up runner finds a clear passage late.
scenarios.body: Eyeeye or Patty O'Farrell, who are genuine hold-up types and have the best form credentials in the field, need a strong enough gallop to reel in leaders; both carry course-distance form at Good going and could deliver a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Annie's Angel is allowed to roll at an unchallenged, very easy tempo and the prominent runners fail to pick up off the bridle.
scenarios.body: With no immediate rival to press it, Annie's Angel could simply steal a march turning in and hold on as others fail to quicken on the flat; the 4yo is on a hat-trick attempt at this course but its STYLE_FIT tag and limited top-level form temper this.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scrimmager Gets Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the race is messy, pace collapses or leaders all tire simultaneously, gifting a midfield-held horse a fortuitous opportunity.
scenarios.body: Highland Earl is the one redistributed runner with a recent winning mark on Good ground at this trip, and Cool Summer has placed at this course; neither is truly at home in mid-pack but a chaotic race could allow them in.

watchPoints.text: Whispering Willow's Keith Donoghue partnership has a strong record in similar conditions — watch for him to position just off Annie's Angel and make a sustained move from 3 out; if he travels with ease to the last, he is very hard to beat.

Annie's Angel sets the whole race's tempo — if she weakens or is headed before 2 out, the entire scenario shifts dramatically, potentially handing a prominent chaser like Victoria Kesia or a late runner like Eyeeye an uncontested run to the line.

With at least eight genuine hold-up types in a 19-runner field, traffic and interference in the home straight is a serious risk — horses like Eyeeye and Patty O'Farrell must find a clear lane or their late runs will be wasted.

Highland Earl returns from 367 days off with a winning form line on Good — watch in the market for any support; Brian Hayes's booking and that winning form make it the one redistributed hold-up runner capable of springing a surprise if sharper than expected.

Syosset is an intriguing watch as a flat-code switcher — three wins over 12f on the all-weather suggest ability, but jumping hurdles on Good ground in a 19-runner field after 290 days off is a very different test and form translators should treat it with caution.

races.name: Roscommon Herald Handicap Hurdle (0-100)

runners_data.name: Double Power
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a fading-in-finish flag; sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 5 Good-ground starts is damning, and from OR 99 off a 45-day break he needs a truly strong gallop that this race is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Fair Damsel
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 1W2P from 15 Good-ground runs and a capable 5lb claimer aboard; the step up to 3m suits her staying profile and she should secure a front-rank position naturally, which is her comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Its Not Over Yet
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up/prominent dual-style operator who has placed at 3m on Good twice in his last two runs; Phillip Enright is an astute jumps jockey and the 37-day freshen-up from OR 97 looks ideal for a staying handicap at this venue.

runners_data.name: Western Model
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed in 5 of his last 5 Good-ground starts without winning; Sean O'Keeffe partners and the 23-day turnaround keeps him sharp — he should be travelling kindly in behind Tradonthebay.

runners_data.name: Where Are You Now
runners_data.note: Unorthodox style flag; Harry Cobden travels over from GB for a 5yo lightly raced on this sort of trip, with only 4 starts and 0 wins or places on Good ground — the form doesn't jump off the page for this marathon trip.

runners_data.name: Tradonthebay
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; his form reads 84-255 suggesting he rarely wins but can travel prominently, and with a 5lb claimer up he is set to bowl along unenthused — more pace-setter than genuine winning force.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: Won over 3m on Good ground and has placed twice more at this trip; P J Rothwell has fired in 3 runners in the last 14 days suggesting the yard is in form, and a 30-day break keeps Mistyburn fresh enough to attack from mid-division.

runners_data.name: Woodie Campelltown
runners_data.note: Fading-in-finish warning applies here; has never won or placed from 4 Good-ground runs and a sim-going record of 0W0P from 2 starts does not inspire confidence at this trip for a 6yo with a patchy profile.

runners_data.name: Chasing Crowns
runners_data.note: Another runner flagged for fading late; despite a recent third over 3m on Good his pattern is inconsistent, and from a true hold-up position at 153lbs there is little in his form to suggest he overcomes the pace shape here.

runners_data.name: Katie's Casper
runners_data.note: Strong-travelling hold-up type by profile, but pushed forward on the race map because of the crowded backmarkers; the 3m trip on Good suits and trainer Dermot McLoughlin has 3 runners in 22 days — active yard angle worth noting even if the positional fit is compromised.

runners_data.name: Written In My Soul
runners_data.note: Has pulled up twice in recent outings including a P on latest; true hold-up runner shown in midfield due to redistribution, and the lack of any wins or places on Good ground from 8 tries makes it hard to make a case here.

runners_data.name: Something Simple
runners_data.note: Jumps record features two pulls-up and an OR-drop to 81; natural backmarker shifted forward on the map due to field compression, and with soft-ground form but no wins on Good this is a tough ask at 3m for a 6yo.

runners_data.name: Road To The Weir
runners_data.note: Veteran of 10 who fades in finishes; natural hold-up horse remapped to midfield, 0 wins and 1 place from 15 Good-ground runs — age, style displacement and fade tendency all point the same way.

runners_data.name: Will It Be You
runners_data.note: 223 days off the track is a significant concern for a 9yo; another true backmarker whose map position overstates his likely proximity to the pace, and a career record of 1 win from 9 Good-ground runs does little to compensate for the layoff.

runners_data.name: Moonshine Girl
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 2 places from 15 Good-ground starts; the 7yo has been placed twice over staying trips and is trained by the same yard as Tradonthebay — worth watching for whether the two stable companions work together tactically.

runners_data.name: Queen Kulina
runners_data.note: 10yo hold-up mare placed on Good ground but showing a 0W2P sim record from 15 tries; remapped from the back due to redistribution and the age profile makes it hard to see her sustaining a challenge at 3m in this competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Barryroe Madam
runners_data.note: Form reads 300-00 which is bleak; despite a win record of 1 and 3 places on Good over career, the recent five runs include nothing better than 3rd and trainer Terence O'Brien has just 1 from 8 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who found 2nd last time over 2m4f on Good; trainer Andrew Slattery has 2 from 32 in 14 days but the step to 3m is new territory — she shapes like a horse who could travel well before stamina becomes the question.

runners_data.name: Tango Theatre
runners_data.note: 11yo veteran with an outstanding 1W5P from 15 Good-ground starts and won over 2m6f on Good last year; jumps economically, travels well in a prominent position and the experience of McConnell's yard makes him a prime beneficiary of this uncontested-pace scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Tradonthebay is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-horse field and, with no obvious challenger for the lead, is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop over this 3m trip on Good ground at Roscommon. The prominent horses — Fair Damsel, Western Model, Tango Theatre, Moonshine Girl and Ladies Well — will fan out behind, creating a compact chasing group rather than a pressured pace scenario, meaning the fractions are unlikely to become genuinely searching until the final circuit. With Tradonthebay able to dictate without being harassed, the race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield gallopers who can travel through the race and challenge from a position of comfort, rather than deep hold-up horses who need a strong pace to bring them into contention late. This field holds considerably more true hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Katie's Casper, Written In My Soul, Something Simple, Road To The Weir, Will It Be You and Queen Kulina are all natural backmarkers redistributed to midfield; the runners most likely to genuinely secure prominent positions are Fair Damsel, Western Model, Tango Theatre and Moonshine Girl, given their consistent pattern of racing close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tradonthebay Sets Steady Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Tradonthebay dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the prominent horses track comfortably without pressure.
scenarios.body: Tradonthebay sets a manageable tempo that keeps the race together until the home turn, at which point those positioned just off the pace — particularly the prominent types with strong Good-ground form — are ideally placed to pounce; horses that travel kindly and strike from the front rank are rewarded.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Grind Out Result
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate but the field compresses, turning the race into an attritional grind from three out.
scenarios.body: The clustered prominent group begin to assert from the third-last hurdle, with stamina becoming the deciding factor over the final 6f; horses with proven 3m credentials and clean jumping on Good ground hold the advantage over those relying on a strong pace to be produced late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply on the final circuit, stringing the field out and catching prominent horses flat-footed.
scenarios.body: A genuine injection of pace on the second circuit burns off the front-rank travellers before the last, leaving a gap for the handful of authentic hold-up horses who have found a clear run; however, this scenario is structurally discounted because most mapped midfielders are redistributed hold-up types unlikely to be in their natural position to deliver a true late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Tradonthebay's unopposed lead is so comfortable that he is never headed and the chasing pack fail to close.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to apply pressure, Tradonthebay effectively jumps his way round and outstays a field that has sat too far back in a slowly-run heat; this is the least likely scenario given Tradonthebay's form figures of 84-255 suggest he is a handicap plodder rather than a dominant front-runner, but the lack of pace opposition keeps it live.

watchPoints.text: Tango Theatre has a 1W5P record on Good ground and settles beautifully in prominent positions — if he travels into contention rounding the home turn, his stamina and jumping accuracy make him the one to beat.

Its Not Over Yet placed twice from his last two over 3m on Good; Phillip Enright will drop him in off a modest pace and his hold-up/prominent flexibility means he can find his own race shape regardless of how Tradonthebay plays it.

Tradonthebay's lone front-running role means his jockey (5lb claimer Jack Gilligan) sets the entire race tempo — if he dawdles, the field will bunch dangerously at the last two hurdles; watch for any sign of the pace quickening heading out on the final circuit.

Mistyburn's trainer P J Rothwell has saddled 3 runners in 14 days suggesting a barn in form, and Mistyburn is a course-distance winner on Good — stable confidence combined with a fresh horse over the right trip is a combination worth monitoring in the market.

With six genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, the interior of this 19-runner field could become dangerously congested from the fourth-last hurdle; watch for scrimmaging on the bend and runners being denied a clear run, particularly those with jockey claims who may lack the experience to find a gap.
